raised_by: todo-metadata-layer roadmap's stored-ref-repair work: 111 -> 474 (+363), proved by corpus_resolution_snapshot.py at 0 lost / 0 moved with all 363 added mappings ground-truthed (0 failed an independent head/close-brace check, 0 targeted a non-tree-unique basename, 22 stratified spot-checks exact at file:line). Both repairs are applied at RESOLUTION time in the new scripts/todo-graph/ref_resolution.py, which lint Check 7's walk AND the identity snapshot both call so they cannot drift. (1) BASENAME REPAIR -- a stored .c/.h path with no directory component that does not exist at the repo root, whose basename is unique among the tree's .c/.h files, is checked against that file (e.g. `boot_desktop.c` -> `src/kernel/main/boot_desktop.c`). It applies to `kind=file` refs as well as `kind=symbol` refs: 673 of the corpus's 1,167 stamped .c/.h FILE refs do not exist at their authored path and 629 are bare and tree-unique, so repairing only symbol refs starved the section-scope pairing of candidates (Codex adversarial, +158 occurrences once fixed). The 8 that remain -- 7 occurrences across 2 ambiguous basenames (`entropy.c`, `entropy.h`) plus 1 for an absent one (`hv_bar.h`) -- are never guessed and stay counted. (2) SECTION-SCOPE PAIRING -- a symbol ref carrying no file of its own is paired to a file when exactly ONE of the files its own TODO SECTION's stamped items author actually defines it; build.py pairs only within an ITEM, so an item whose sibling item named the file loses a pairing the section really does carry. One false positive surfaced by the new visibility was fixed at its cause rather than marked: `return <bare identifier>;` is no longer read as a stub when the identifier names a file-scope VARIABLE in the same translation unit, because that is an accessor reading state (compositor_get_test_seed at src/kernel/main/compositor.c:64), not a placeholder; `return STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED;` still fires and neither a macro nor an enum constant can satisfy the exemption. The one genuine stub it found (test_usermode_color_active, the release-flavor no-op inline) got the existing INTENTIONAL-STUB marker.
why: Check 7 can only inspect a stamped symbol it can RESOLVE; an unresolved ref yields no finding, so losing resolution is indistinguishable from passing. This number is the floor: a drop is an ERROR (rc 7). Raising it is the point -- when the resolver improves, update this file in the same commit and say what changed. This file is TRACKED state and is enforced fail-CLOSED (rc 8) when missing or malformed; STUB_LINT_ALLOW_NO_BASELINE=1 is the deliberate, reported bypass. `total` is enforced too: the floor is a RATIO, so a shrinking denominator would let refs lost from the cache read as an improved ratio (rc 7 on any move, in either direction).
standing_gap: 1,152 occurrences not resolved, in evidence-shaped buckets that deliberately do NOT claim a cause: unpaired-ref 859 (down from 1,122 -- a symbol named with no file to look in, and none of its section's authored files defines it), calllike-unresolved 132 and no-calllike-token 89 (both UP from 35/47, because the repairs moved refs INTO the population that gets looked at: a repaired ref whose symbol is not defined in the repaired file now lands in a visible bucket instead of being dropped before counting), missing-file 8 (down from 246 -- 7 occurrences across 2 ambiguous basenames `entropy.c`/`entropy.h`, plus 1 for the absent `hv_bar.h`), non-c-suffix 63, path-escape 1. The names describe what was observed, not why: a call site, a prototype and a macro invocation all carry a call-like token while the real definition lives in another file.
largest_recoverable_class: unpaired-ref, at 859 occurrences, remains the largest class and is NOT straightforwardly recoverable. MEASURED 2026-08-06: 673 of the 736 unique unpaired symbols do have exactly one C definition tree-wide (1,028 occurrences), but binding on tree-wide name uniqueness alone was REJECTED for this roadmap with reason -- a bare unique-name search can bind an unrelated same-named definition in a different link product with no way to prove linkage, and the one narrow existing use of tree-wide basename uniqueness (follow_declaration's sibling rule) is an explicitly accepted risk paid for by hand-verifying all 18 of its mappings. 673 is 37x that and unverifiable at section scale. The authored scope evidence that would make it provable does not exist in this corpus either: exactly 1 of 232 TODO nodes carries a `file_patterns` frontmatter list, and it holds zero unpaired refs. What section scope could reach, it reached. The residual names a symbol with no file anywhere in its section, which is an authoring convention (prose naming an API) rather than bad stored data, and is a COUNTING-contract question, not an extractor bug.
